items: Stabilize the Daycare Crisis: Send a written message to your provider that acknowledges her experience, signals partnership, and requests a 45-minute structured meeting within seven days.

Stabilize the Daycare Crisis: Draft a one-page meeting agenda that includes an opening team statement, space for her observations, your home intervention updates, a co-regulation plan, and a 30-day review date.
Stabilize the Daycare Crisis: Email the meeting agenda to your provider at least 24 hours before the conversation so she has time to prepare and feels included as a collaborator.
Stabilize the Daycare Crisis: Avoid promising specific timelines for when biting will stop and refuse any language suggesting voluntary withdrawal while you work on the problem.
Build Home Intervention: Practice consistent co-regulation responses at home so your toddler begins associating the same calming phrases that daycare staff will use during incidents.
Build Home Intervention: Log each biting incident with time, location, preceding activity, and emotional state to identify patterns and triggers that you can address proactively.
Build Home Intervention: Create a calm-down corner in your home with sensory tools like a weighted lap pad or textured balls where your toddler can practice releasing frustration safely.
Build Home Intervention: Schedule a pediatric check-in specifically to discuss impulse control development and rule out any underlying issues like hearing problems or speech delays.
Protect Your Foundation: Set a hard cutoff time for Googling parenting advice each night so you can rest instead of spiraling into anxiety-driven research until midnight.
Protect Your Foundation: Schedule one intentional 30-minute connection with your partner this week that has nothing to do with childcare, daycare, or the biting problem.
Protect Your Foundation: Give yourself one non-negotiable five-minute recovery break each day, whether in your car, a closet, or a bathroom, before picking up your child.
Protect Your Foundation: Remind yourself daily that toddler impulse control is a developmental milestone under construction, not a character flaw you failed to prevent.
